title: Capacity of the general two-user interference channel
formal: Determine \(F_{\mathrm{IC}}(\mathrm{W},\lambda )=\sup _{(R_{1},R_{2})\in C_{\mathrm{IC}}(\mathrm{W})}[\lambda R_{1}+(1- \lambda )R_{2}]\) for every finite-alphabet discrete memoryless two-user interference channel W and every real \(\lambda \in [0,1]\), with independent private messages and no feedback, in the model below.
context:
Two sender–receiver pairs share a channel, but each sender initially knows only its own independent message. This separates interference from broadcasting, where one encoder knows both messages. The full rate tradeoff matters because improving one receiver’s rate can reduce the other’s.

The weighted capacity function describes all supporting directions of the capacity region. The fixed numerical tolerance makes the desired approximation explicit without imposing a one-letter formula or restricting the coding scheme. The original Han–Kobayashi reference supplies a fundamental inner bound, not a general matching converse. Gaussian interference is a separately significant continuous-alphabet model, and discretizing it requires its own approximation argument.
why: A canonical unresolved network-information-theory model in which independent communications compete through interference.

definitions: A channel consists of nonempty finite alphabets \(X_{1},X_{2},Y_{1},Y_{2}\) and real probabilities \(\mathrm{W}(y_{1},y_{2}|x_{1},x_{2})\ge 0\) summing to one over \((y_{1},y_{2})\) for each input pair. Conditional on the input sequences, n uses have product law \(\prod _{t=1}^{n} \mathrm{W}(y_{1},t,y_{2},t|x_{1},t,x_{2},t)\). Messages \(M_{i}\) are independent and uniform on \(\{1,\ldots ,K_{i},n\}\). Encoder i is a deterministic map from its own message to \(X_{i}^{n}\); receiver i uses a deterministic decoder \(Y_{i}^{n}\to \{1,\ldots ,K_{i},n\}\). Error is the probability that at least one receiver estimates its message incorrectly, averaged over both messages and channel randomness. A nonnegative pair \((R_{1},R_{2})\) is achievable when codes on block lengths \(n_{j}\to \infty\) have error tending to zero and \(\liminf _{j} (\log _{2}K_{i},n_{j})/n_{j}\ge R_{i}\) for \(i=1,2\). \(C_{\mathrm{IC}}(\mathrm{W})\) is the closure of achievable pairs. Both codebooks and W are known at all terminals. There is no common message, output feedback, transmitter or receiver cooperation, input cost or computational restriction. Predetermined time sharing is allowed. The region is compact, convex and downward closed; its nonnegative supporting values for \(\lambda \in [0,1]\) determine it exactly. \(F_{\mathrm{IC}}\) is measured in bits per joint channel use. The task quantifies over arbitrary real channel laws as mathematical objects; no finite-precision input or algorithmic evaluation model is imposed.
answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous real-valued function g on every channel W defined below and every real \(\lambda \in [0,1]\), and prove in Lean that |\(g- F_{\mathrm{IC}}(\mathrm{W},\lambda )|\le 1/100\) pointwise throughout that domain, in the units stated in the definitions. The answer must establish lower and upper bounds with this uniform error guarantee. An exact determination also qualifies. A finite set of sample values, an uncertified plot, or a restatement of the defining optimization or limit does not determine the curve. No predetermined formula grammar or polynomial evaluation-time requirement is imposed. This numerical acceptance criterion does not assert exact equality with a conjectured curve.

sentences: Two independent senders transmit private messages to separate receivers through one interference channel.
Each encoder sees only its own message and has no output feedback.
The target is the weighted supporting function of the capacity region for every finite channel and weight.
Lean acceptance requires absolute error at most 0.01 bits per joint channel use throughout this domain.
A coding inner bound or a limit over arbitrary block codes without a determination at the required accuracy does not answer the full question.
